entries.name: mcp__cfo__inspect_pages
entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (list) or (read).

Reads the workspace page tree, each page's visible block order, saved table settings, and reusable references, without changing anything. Named pages come back in the order you named them, not sidebar order; blocks come back in page order. Returned page references and block guide_targets identify saved objects; a guide target is the value a guide step's anchor takes. They do not certify Canvas element visibility. scenario defaults to the scenario in view. Legacy chart inspection returns configuration, not calculated chart values; numbers come from saved tables or the underlying variables.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

as_of_point.description: Optional snapshot with exactly one point type. Absence selects the current state.

calendar_boundary.description: A local calendar period boundary in the user's runtime timezone, for phrases such as "yesterday" or "last month"; UTC when no timezone is known.

offset.description: 0 is the current period, -1 the previous, 1 the next.

change_log_id.description: Exact or approximate changelog point. The backend resolves to this workspace's latest changelog at or before this ID.

relative_duration.description: A duration from now, such as "a couple hours ago" or "a day from now"; a day is 24 hours and a week is seven days.

timestamp.description: Exact instant supplied by the user, runtime context, or a tool result, as RFC3339 or RFC3339Nano with a timezone.

after.description: The previous result's next.after value; the list continues after that page, under the same scenario and target.

limit.description: Maximum page summaries to return; the default is 25.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

contains.description: Text to find, ignoring case. Each page comes back with only the text blocks whose text contains it, each with its Markdown, ref, and target; tables and other blocks are left out.

include_text.description: Adds each text block's content as Markdown, the form edit_pages add_text and update_text take.

target.description: Pages to read by name or a returned qualified target. A name matching nothing does not fail the call: the pages that exist are returned, and unmatched names are listed in a trailing unresolved entry.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.
Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

schema1.description: Page names or returned qualified targets to list. An absent or empty list includes every page. Unmatched names appear in unresolved_page_names without failing the call. Named pages follow resolution order, not sidebar order.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: list, read. Fields beside the block apply to it: as_of_point, scenario.

entries.name: mcp__cfo__inspect_table_blocks
entries.description:
Input constraint: Provide parameters for exactly one of: (bounds) or (compare) or (dimension) or (items) or (list) or (read) or (variable).

Lists saved tables (a summary each, or the full layout of tables named in target), reads selected cells, or compares saved states. One read returns several scenarios side by side when comparison names them. Rows and columns are objects with reusable refs. Rows carry formulas by range, bare values in column order, writability, and hidden-child counts; cell exceptions carry value and cell_formula. Columns carry the variable or dimension, grain, and date range; ranges defines each range once. Rows and columns are selected by inspected ref, unambiguous name, or coordinate predicate; depth controls descendants. include_edit_rules adds owned defaults and accepted actions. items and bounds inspect a dimension with or without a table target. references names the properties returned formulas use. variable and dimension inspect named objects and their dependents, or list them all. Unreadable evidence stays explicit. Reads never change the model. Omitted format uses json; an explicit format overrides it for this call.

_context.description: Optional active scenario, page, and time zone.

before_change_log_id.description: The earlier saved change to compare against. The comparison names rows removed or added since it under row_membership.

page.description: Limit a table list to this existing page.

target.description: Saved tables by name or ref, one or a list. Named tables come back in full: layout, signature, presentation, and property homes. Omission lists every table as a summary of row and column counts, first rows, and window; names that match nothing are reported under unresolved.

org_id.description: Workspace ID or slug. Optional when you belong to one workspace. Otherwise, call list_orgs and choose an ID or slug. Numbers always identify workspace IDs.

measures.description: Values per compared scenario: VALUE, DELTA (difference from the selected scenario), PERCENT (percent difference). Defaults to VALUE.

scenarios.description: Existing scenarios to read beside the selected scenario, by name or inspected reference.

comparison.description: For action read. saved uses the saved comparison; none reads underlying values and formulas; an object compares the selected scenario with each named scenario in this one read, whatever the table saves. Defaults to saved. The saved table is unchanged.

grain.description: Reads the table's Date periods rolled up to this coarser grain without changing the saved table; the grain the table already shows is its plain read. Each period holds what the model calculates at that grain: a variable's time rollup (its base periods summed, closed, or averaged) or a timeless formula recomputed there; a variable with neither reads blank. Rolled-up period columns are read-only; the saved table's own columns take writes.

recalculate.description: Calculates the table from scratch, ignoring every cached or reused result, and makes that calculation the cached one so the page shows it too. Use it when a value disagrees with what the person sees, with another read, or with arithmetic you can check; the result's recalculated says whether the cached result differed. Needs comparison none: a saved or requested comparison refuses it. Costs a full calculation; not for routine reads.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

after.description: The previous page's next.after; it continues the same target, or the listing at the object and definition where that page stopped, at the same snapshot.

after_2.description: Grid continuations bind table, selection, scenario and snapshot. Focused next binds its definition page and snapshot. For items, copy the prior member spelling, including an empty string. For list, copy next.after.

as_of_point.description: Optional snapshot with exactly one point type. Absence selects the current state.

calendar_boundary.description: A local calendar period boundary in the user's runtime timezone, for phrases such as "yesterday" or "last month"; UTC when no timezone is known.

offset.description: 0 is the current period, -1 the previous, 1 the next.

change_log_id.description: Exact or approximate changelog point. The backend resolves to this workspace's latest changelog at or before this ID.

relative_duration.description: A duration from now, such as "a couple hours ago" or "a day from now"; a day is 24 hours and a week is seven days.

timestamp.description: Exact instant supplied by the user, runtime context, or a tool result, as RFC3339 or RFC3339Nano with a timezone.

columns.description: Column references as a read prints them, unambiguous names, a member by its path from its variable or its axis dimension, one bracket per breakdown level, or native coordinate predicates; a name in backticks selects the same column as the name without them. Omission includes the saved columns; explicit columns take precedence over periods.

period_range.description: Inclusive system Date interval at the saved axis grain, with bounds in that grain's period spelling, such as 2026-07 through 2026-09 for month.

conditions.description: Filter stored formula definitions by readable conditions. Omission includes every saved definition.

depth.description: Descendant levels relative to selected rows, or saved roots when rows are omitted. With rows, omission returns those rows only; without rows, omission leaves the full saved tree eligible.

dimension.description: Existing workspace dimension by name or inspected reference, including imported dimensions before table placement.

format.description: Optional compact JSON or addressed REAM encoding override. Omission uses the workspace's current default encoding.

formula_origins.description: Each row or column already carries its formula per range under formulas, a cell that breaks that rule says so in the cell, and a row or column computed by a rule saved outside this table's nodes names that rule's owner and condition in inherited_from. Omission is off; a selection of exactly one cell defaults to all. zeros adds rules to rows containing a zero, blank, or error: every rule the engine ranked for the row, best first, with the ones that computed a cell marked selected. all adds rules to every row.

include_edit_rules.description: Adds each returned row's and column's editing rules: the actions the edit input accepts there, its owned Actuals and Forecast defaults with ownership and writability, and its formula roles. Omission returns writability alone; a refused write reports the rules it broke.

include_inputs.description: Expands one level of formula inputs beneath the selected rows. With one cell selected by rows and columns and comparison none, also explains its input values and sources. Input rows and evidence share the response budget.

limit.description: Saved formula definitions per page, default 100. A scope can span pages; next continues it. An oversized formula returns unavailable coverage instead of truncated text.

limit_2.description: Maximum grid rows, items, or listed tables (500), or saved formula definitions (100). Defaults: grid 500, items 50, tables 100, formula definitions 100. Grid parents and descendants count separately. The response budget may stop earlier; calculation inputs stay complete.

periods.description: boundaries returns only the first and last period of each range (where Actuals end and Forecast begins) and of the window, without changing the saved table. An explicit column selection takes precedence.

rows.description: Row references as a read prints them, unambiguous names or full paths, a member by its path from its variable or its axis dimension, one bracket per breakdown level (Revenue[West], Revenue[West][Enterprise], Employee ID[E-207], and Revenue[empty:None] for the member with no value), or native coordinate predicates; a name in backticks selects the same row as the name without them. Matches are deduplicated in saved order. Omission leaves the saved tree eligible. A read that names rows or columns holds every member of the layout, zero and empty members included, whatever the saved display hides; a read that names none shows what the app displays.

period_range.description: Inclusive system Date interval at the saved axis grain, with bounds in that grain's period spelling, such as 2026-07 through 2026-09 for month.

scenario.description: Scenario to use. Defaults to the scenario in view, which can change between turns.

source_health.description: Source status detail. Compact is the default.

target.description: Optional saved table that must contain the dimension. Without it, the read covers imported or manual members before any table exists.

target_2.description: A workspace-wide variable or dimension reference, or a list of them, including at a historical snapshot. A list answers with one entry per reference in the order given, each source query stated once under sources, and a reference that matches nothing refused in its own entry. Omission lists every readable variable or dimension in the scenario as the same entries, in saved order, with next continuing the listing.

input_schema.description: Fill exactly one action block: bounds, compare, dimension, items, list, read, variable. Fields beside the block apply to it: scenario.

With about an hour left before 5:52 PM, I'm sketching a small plan module that reads the business plan JSON and computes a per-investigation spend limit from team pricing, target margin, worker costs, and investigation volume.

I'm designing a Meter class to track cumulative spend against that limit, then wiring it into the lineup logic so a stop callback can halt deliberation early and record why nobody was named, falling through to the existing "no match" exit path that lets investigation continue.

I need to prevent the resume logic from restarting a lineup if the stop reason was specifically the spend limit, so I'll use a recognizable prefix on that note to detect it. For `fix()`, I'll check the meter before each retry attempt and abort further tries once the budget's exhausted, skipping the harm check and verification replays in that case, with both `fix()` and the lineup pulling the meter through args like the existing tracer pattern. For actually computing spend, I'm leaning on neatroots-traced replays rather than agent-printed tokens, since not all replays get traced that way.

If neatroots can't be queried, I'll just treat spend as unknown and continue rather than stopping, noting this once. There's also a lag issue since replay counts show up in neatroots only after the round finishes, so the spend check will always be a round behind -- that's acceptable to document. I'm sketching out the record's spend section (limit, source, whether it was raised, amount spent, and what stopped it), plus a `--spend-limit` CLI flag that overrides the plan's default and marks `raised: true` if it's higher. Finally, I'm planning three tests: one for reading the limit from the plan file, one for a run that crosses the limit mid-execution, and more.

I could test this at the CLI level without neatroots by monkeypatching it to raise NeatError so spent falls back to allowance. That raises the question of whether `--spend-limit` should also apply to the investigate command, since the user implied investigate takes it as a default.

For `lineup` it should be optional with no default (None means no metering), while for investigate the default should come from `pitch/plan.json` when it exists, otherwise falling back to no limit. I'm also sketching out the Meter dataclass with limit, case_id, allowance, and windows fields to track metered usage across stretches.

Finishing up the Meter class: adding tracking for start time, source file, raised flag, and an ask callback, plus a spent() method that queries replay costs matching the case ID and sums with the allowance, and a why() method that formats a message when spending exceeds the limit.

I'm checking whether neatroots() is actually reachable in tests since it's running live on this machine -- tests shouldn't depend on the real service, so the ask callable needs to be monkeypatched. I'm also tracking down where args.meter gets constructed: inside investigate() before the run, and inside lineup() when a spend limit is passed.

I'm planning a `_meter(args, case, record)` helper in cli, with checks in `_investigate` after lineup step and in fix() between attempts, plus saving record["spend"] at the end. I also want the case page's timeline to surface a "stopped at spend limit" note, so I need to look at the casefile timeline rendering around lines 125-180 before touching the lineup() and record-saving code.

def fix(args) -> int:
    """Apply the ruling on a branch and replay until the fix clears the bar or plainly does not. If it does not, try again.

    The bar: the fix commit's failure rate is 95% likely to be back within 5 points of the rate
    before the culprit. A patch that does not clear it gets one more try, with the first patch
    and its failing replays in front of the model. If that does not clear it either, the culprit
    is reverted, which is the safe answer and loses what the commit was for. Every try is kept
    in the record.
    """
    loaded = _need_culprit(args)
    if loaded is None:
        return 2
    case, repo, record, path = loaded
    if not record.get("ruling"):
        print(f"No ruling yet. Run `whodunit ruling {args.case}` first.")
        return 2
    wanted = record["ruling"]["ruling"]
    began = _now_ms()
    attempts = [_attempt(wanted, case, repo, record, args, number=1)]
    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):

        feedback = (first.get("note") or "") + "\nThe first patch:\n" + first.get("diff", "none was made") + "\nReplays of it that still failed:\n" + "\n".join(first.get("failed_replays", []) or ["none recorded
        if (first.get("harm") or {}).get("broken"):
            feedback += "\nThe first patch cleared its own case and made other requests go wrong more often than before it. " + _harm_said(first["harm"]) + " A patch must not do that."
        print("  The patch " + ("made other requests worse" if (first.get("harm") or {}).get("broken") else "did not clear the bar") + ". Trying once more, with the first patch and what went wrong in view.")
        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.PATCH, case, repo, record, args, feedback, number=2))
    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):
        print("  The second patch is not kept either. Falling back to a revert, which loses what the commit was for.")
        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.REVERT, case, repo, record, args, number=3))

    final = next((a for a in reversed(attempts) if _proven(a)), attempts[-1])
    record["fix"] = final
    record["attempts"] = attempts

def check(args) -> int:
    """Replay a kept case against a ref. This is the regression test."""
    import time

    case = Case.load(args.case)
    repo = Path(args.repo).resolve()
    ref = args.ref or case.fixed or "HEAD"
    began = _now_ms()
    with Runner(repo, case) as runner:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, args.parallel)) as pool:
            verdicts = list(pool.map(lambda _: runner.trial(ref), range(args.runs)))
    failures, judged = verdicts.count(FAIL), verdicts.count(FAIL) + verdicts.count(PASS)
    sha = resolve(repo, ref)
    print(f"{case.id} at {sha[:12]}: {failures} failures in {judged} replays." + (f" {verdicts.count(VOID)} more were voided by provider errors." if VOID in verdicts else ""))
    path = record_path(args)
    record = load_record(path)
    if record:
        record.setdefault("checks", []).append({"at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "ref": sha, "runs": judged, "failures": failures})
        _replayed(record, began)
        save_record(path, record)
    return 0 if failures == 0 and judged > 0 and "skip" not in verdicts else 1

def spend_limit(plan: dict) -> float:
    """The most one investigation may spend, in dollars, if the plan's margin on a Team agent is to hold.

        limit = (team price x (1 - target margin) - worker cost / agents per worker) / investigations included

    A Team agent pays the price each month. Keeping the margin leaves price x (1 - margin) for
    serving it. Its share of a replay worker comes off that, and the rest is spread over the
    investigations the tier includes, as if all of them were used. An investigation that stays
    under this cannot be the one that breaks the margin.

class Meter:

    Replays are priced the way the damages are: token counts from the runs' model spans in
    neatroots, at list prices. The model calls for the brief and the patch are not metered, so
    the plan's allowance for them is counted as spent from the start. A replay still being
    written to neatroots is not counted yet, so the meter runs a few replays behind.

    unknown: str = ""  # why the replays could not be priced, if neatroots could not be asked
    stopped: str = ""  # the step that was stopped, once one has been

    def spent(self) -> float:
        stretches = [*self.windows, [self.started_ms, time.time() * 1000 + 60000]]
        mine = REPLAY.format(like=f"%case:{self.case_id}%".replace("'", "''"))
        mine += " and (" + " or ".join(f"(r.started_ms >= {float(lo)} and r.started_ms <= {float(hi)})" for lo, hi in stretches) + ")"

"""The business plan sets a spend limit, and an investigation that reaches it stops and says so."""

import json

import pytest

from tests.planted import stub_history
from tests.test_lineup import flaky
from whodunit import casefile
from whodunit.cli import load_record, main
from whodunit.lineup import statistical_bisect
from whodunit.neat import NeatError
from whodunit.plan import REACHED, Meter, meter_for, read_plan, spend_limit

PLAN = {"team_price_usd": 249, "team_investigations_included": 40, "target_margin": 0.7639, "worker_monthly_cost_usd": 61,
        "team_agents_per_shared_worker": 15, "brief_and_patch_cost_per_investigation_usd": 0.2}


class Spent:
    """Stands in for neatroots: every question about replays gets these token counts back."""

    def __init__(self, prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int = 0):
        self.rows = [{"model": "claude-haiku", "pt": prompt_tokens, "ct": completion_tokens}]

    def call(self, tool, **arguments):
        return {"rows": self.rows}


def test_the_limit_is_read_from_the_plan_file(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "plan.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(PLAN))
    # (249 x (1 - 0.7639) - 61 / 15) / 40
    assert spend_limit(read_plan(path)) == pytest.approx(1.37)
    assert spend_limit({**PLAN, "target_margin": 0.5}) == pytest.approx(3.01)
    meter = meter_for("c", {"replay_windows": [[1, 2]]}, path=path)
    assert meter.limit == pytest.approx(1.37) and meter.allowance == 0.2 and meter.source == str(path) and not meter.raised and meter.windows == [[1, 2]]
    raised = meter_for("c", {}, given=5.0, path=path)
    assert raised.limit == 5.0 and raised.raised and raised.source == "--spend-limit"
    assert not meter_for("c", {}, given=1.0, path=path).raised  # lowering it is not raising it
    assert meter_for("c", {}, path=tmp_path / "none.json") is None and read_plan(tmp_path / "none.json") is None


def test_the_plan_in_the_repo_gives_the_limit_the_readme_quotes():
    plan = read_plan()
    assert plan["team_price_usd"] == 249 and plan["team_investigations_included"] == 40
    assert spend_limit(plan) == pytest.approx(1.37)


def test_the_meter_prices_replays_like_the_damages_and_counts_the_allowance():
    under = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=lambda: Spent(1_000_000))  # $1.00 of replays
    assert under.spent() == pytest.approx(1.20) and under.why() == ""
    over = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=lambda: Spent(1_000_000, 40_000))  # $1.20 of replays
    assert over.why() == f"{REACHED}: about $1.40 spent of $1.37 allowed"

    def down():
        raise NeatError("connection refused")
    blind = Meter(limit=1.37, case_id="c", allowance=0.2, ask=down)
    assert blind.why() == "" and "connection refused" in blind.to_dict()["note"]


def test_a_lineup_that_would_cross_the_limit_stops_and_names_nobody():
    asked = []

    def stop() -> str:
        asked.append(1)
        return f"{REACHED}: about $1.40 spent of $1.37 allowed" if len(asked) > 2 else ""
    found = statistical_bisect(40, flaky(25, 0.3, seed=3), budget=400, stop=stop)
    assert found.culprit is None and found.note.startswith(REACHED)
    assert found.replays < 40 and len(found.remaining) > 1  # handed back with the suspects still in play
    free = statistical_bisect(40, flaky(25, 0.3, seed=3), budget=400)
    assert free.culprit == 25 and free.replays > found.replays


def test_the_record_says_why_a_lineup_stopped_and_when_the_limit_was_raised(tmp_path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    def down():
        raise NeatError("not running")
    monkeypatch.setattr("whodunit.plan.neatroots", down)
    made = stub_history(tmp_path / "repo", suspects=12, culprit=5, broken=(3,))
    assert main(["lineup", str(made["case"]), "--repo", str(made["repo"]), "--budget", "60", "--spend-limit", "0"]) == 1
    assert "Stopped: the spend limit was reached" in capsys.readouterr().out
    record = load_record(made["case"].with_suffix(".record.json"))
    assert record["lineup"]["culprit"] is None and record["lineup"]["note"].startswith(REACHED)
    assert len(record["lineup"]["remaining"]) > 1 and all("probability" in s for s in record["lineup"]["remaining"])
    assert record["spend"]["stopped"] == "lineup" and record["spend"]["limit_usd"] == 0 and record["spend"]["from"] == "--spend-limit"
    assert ("spend", "Stopped during the lineup at the spend limit: about $0.00 spent of $0.00 allowed, a limit set by --spend-limit.") in casefile.timeline(record)
    # With room to spend, the same case names its culprit and the record says nothing stopped it.
    assert main(["lineup", str(made["case"]), "--repo", str(made["repo"]), "--budget", "60", "--spend-limit", "50"]) == 0
    record = load_record(made["case"].with_suffix(".record.json"))
    assert record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"] == made["culprit"] and record["spend"]["stopped"] == ""
EOF

# The demo video

`whodunit-demo.mp4` is 2 minutes 16 seconds, 1920 by 1080, with a narrator, captions and a synthesized score. It runs thirteen scenes: the question, one failing run, a title card, the command, the lineup, the motive, the fix, before and after, the trace and the damage, the sealed eval, the plan, the

The narration is a synthesized voice, made with ElevenLabs from the script in `build_film.py`. Each scene is as long as its narration clip, and the events in a scene fire where the words fall.

An earlier cut, 89 seconds with captions and no voice, is kept beside it as `whodunit-v1-captions-only.mp4`.

What is here is the part of the film that is ours:

- `film.json`: the thirteen scenes, their timing in beats, the captions and the camera moves.
- `build_film.py`: the narration script, and the code that times every scene to its clip.
- `screens.tsx`: Whodunit's screens rebuilt so each row and mark can move: the git log, one failing run, the command, the lineup, the Entire checkpoint, the two exhibits, the two fix attempts, before and after, the neatlogs trace, the damages, the docket cards, the cash chart and the three tools.
- `data.json`: the 57 suspects, the ordinary runs and the four replay rounds of the headline case, copied from its record.
- `contact-sheet.png`: sixteen stills from the last third of the film.

The motion template the film runs on is not in the repo, because it is not ours to publish.

## What is real and what is drawn

Every number is from a case record, the cfo.ai model or the neatlogs dashboard. The request and the reply in the chat scene are word for word from the failing run. The lineup plays the record's own four rounds.

The screens are redrawn, so they are not screenshots. The exhibit steps are shortened. The trace shows 13 of the run's 17 steps. The cash chart is drawn from the model's monthly figures and is not cfo.ai's own chart.

### $NOW, Monday: a new mark, and the submission text

The owner asked, mid-session, for the logo to change on the pages and in the film, because the old one was just an x in a ring.

Not checked: nobody has watched the new render at speed. I looked at two stills, the title card at 16 seconds and the close at 133. EOF
